listenings.text: Hello, this is Ray Collins, the site supervisor. Here is the plan for tomorrow. Karen is our field engineer this month, and this is how her day works. She starts at six thirty, and she reads the schedule with me in the office. After that she inspects the north tunnel with two colleagues from the crew. She does not write the report in the morning. She writes it at four o'clock, and she sends it to me before five. She carries the radio all day, so call her any time. Thank you, and have a safe shift.

Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. You asked me about my day here, so here it is. I am a field engineer, so I work outside most of the time. My day starts with the schedule: I read it, and then I talk to my supervisor. My first task is always the same. I inspect the tunnel wall with the crew, every morning, before the machines start. My colleague Tom is different. He works in the office, and he does not go down the tunnel. He prepares the daily report, and I send him the numbers at four. See you on Friday.

extra_audio.text: Karen arrives at the site at six thirty. She reads the schedule with her supervisor. Then she inspects the tunnel wall with two colleagues. At four o'clock she writes the daily report. Her supervisor reads the report the same evening.

reading.rtitle: A Day in the Life of a Field Engineer
paras: Karen Booth is a field engineer on a metro project. She works outside most of the day, so she is not at her desk very often. Her day starts at six thirty, before the crew arrives at the site.
First, she reads the schedule with her supervisor. The schedule says what happens and when. Then she gets her first task of the day: she inspects the tunnel wall with two colleagues.
Karen does not work alone, and she does not stay in one place. She talks to a colleague every hour, on the radio or at the gate, and she walks about eight kilometers before lunch.

At four o'clock she goes back to the office and writes the daily report. The report is short, only one page, and her supervisor reads it the same evening. Karen says: "The best part of my day is the tunnel, not the desk."
